target_claim: For every nonconstant polynomial F in \mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_r] and every prime p, the number c_p(F) of zeros of F modulo p satisfies c_p(F) \leq \deg(F)p^{r-1}.
source_quote: \textbf{\textit{Zippel-Schwartz upper bound.}} \emph{For all primes $p$ we have $c_p(F) \leq \deg(F) \, p^{r-1}$.}
